introduction: This intermediate tier explores the nuanced, day-to-day ethical applications in a teacher's life. It covers the NCTE Code of Professional Ethics, the absolute necessity of student confidentiality, and maintaining professional boundaries.

core_concepts.title: NCTE Code of Professional Ethics
core_concepts.description:
The National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) outlines a teacher's ethical obligations toward four distinct groups:
1. Toward Students: Fostering inclusive education, ensuring safety, and avoiding public shaming.
2. Toward Parents: Maintaining transparent, respectful communication without treating parents condescendingly.
3. Toward Society: Acting as a role model of constitutional values (secularism, equality) and avoiding divisive communal behavior.
4. Toward the Profession: Engaging in Continuous Professional Development (CPD) and not undermining colleagues.

core_concepts.title: Confidentiality and Data Privacy
core_concepts.description:
A core ethical mandate. Teachers have access to highly sensitive information (grades, learning disabilities, family financial issues, medical history). 
- Ethical Rule: This information must NEVER be discussed in the staff room as gossip, shared with other students, or used to shame the child. It must only be shared with authorized personnel (school counselor, principal, or parents) on a strict 'need-to-know' basis.

core_concepts.title: Boundary Maintenance
core_concepts.description:
Teachers must maintain a warm, approachable, but strictly professional boundary with students. 
- Over-involvement: A teacher acting as a student's 'best friend', sharing inappropriate personal secrets, or showing extreme favoritism breaches professional boundaries.
- Under-involvement: Ignoring a child's cries for help or emotional distress breaches the duty of care.

core_concepts.title: Ethical Management of Diversity
core_concepts.description: In an inclusive classroom, treating everyone 'exactly the same' (blindness to background) is unethical. A highly ethical teacher practices **Equity**—recognizing the systemic disadvantages faced by marginalized groups (SEDGs, Dalits, Tribals, religious minorities, CWSN) and actively modifying their pedagogy to support them, avoiding any form of microaggression.

important_entities.name: Microaggressions in the Classroom
important_entities.key_fact: Subtle, everyday actions or insults that marginalize students.
important_entities.significance: Constantly mispronouncing a minority student's name, expressing surprise when a Dalit student speaks excellent English, or assigning cleaning tasks exclusively to girls are ethical breaches. A teacher must be culturally competent enough to recognize and eliminate their own subconscious biases.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will propose a scenario: 'A student steals a pencil. The teacher makes him stand in front of the class and apologize to teach him a moral lesson.' This is **UNETHICAL**. Public shaming destroys the child's self-esteem and violates their dignity. Disciplinary matters must be handled privately and restoratively, not punitively.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: S P S P (Students, Parents, Society, Profession)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember SPSP to recall the four groups a teacher is ethically answerable to according to NCTE.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks how to deal with a student's poor performance, any option that involves reading the student's marks out loud to the whole class is incorrect due to a breach of **Confidentiality and Dignity**.
